# 147 — explainer (HIGH tier: full walkthrough + quiz)

**Item**: ship the minified bundles the site already builds, and un-blind `npm test`
**Branch**: `claude/loop-147` · **Verifier**: PASS, 9/9 criteria independently re-derived, tier **HIGH**
**Diff**: 3 product lines (`home.html` ×2, `plan.html` ×1) + 1 `package.json` test-chain entry + 1 new test file

---

## Goal

Make `home.html` and `plan.html` load the minified JS bundles the repo already generates, minifies, and
commits on every CI run — and, as a direct consequence, let `npm test` run past file 6 of its chain
again.

## The intuition

Backlog 053 built a minify pipeline: `minify-assets.js` turns `planner.js` and `translations.js` into
`planner.min.js` / `translations.min.js`, the daily `sitemap-update.yml` run regenerates **and commits**
them, and `test_minified_assets.js` guards that the committed outputs are byte-fresh. All of that
machinery has been running correctly and daily.

It just wasn't plugged in. At some point `home.html` and `plan.html` drifted back to `src="planner.js"`
/ `src="translations.js"` — the raw sources — so the pipeline has been producing bundles that **nothing
loaded**. The comment sitting directly above the offending line still said *"Minified in CI (backlog
053); edit planner.js, never planner.min.js"*: the comment described the intended wiring, the `src`
below it did not match.

Two consequences, one cause:

1. **Prod shipped ~159 KB of avoidable uncompressed JS on `home.html`** — the shell that serves
   `?pool=` / `?token=` / `?chain=`, i.e. the north-star surface — and ~138 KB on `plan.html`. Both
   tags are static `<script defer>`, so every visitor paid, including SEO landers.

   | File | raw | min | saved |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `planner.js` → `planner.min.js` | 238,585 B | 100,417 B | 138,168 B |
   | `translations.js` → `translations.min.js` | 90,310 B | 69,645 B | 20,665 B |

2. **`npm test` was blind past position 6.** `package.json`'s `test` is one `&&` chain of ~90 files;
   `test_minified_assets.js` is 6th, it exited 1 on unmodified `main`, so **~85 downstream tests never
   ran**. Eleven consecutive build loops (117.2, 125, 128, 130, 137–140, 143, 144, 146) each proved the
   red was pre-existing and correctly declined to fix it as scope creep — so each of them hand-ran its
   own tests one file at a time. Nobody had classified the red: it was not a grumpy test, it was the
   test correctly reporting that prod served the wrong files.

## What changed, in reading order

1. **`home.html:175`** — `<script defer src="translations.js">` → `translations.min.js`.
2. **`home.html:196`** — `<script defer src="planner.js">` → `planner.min.js`. Surrounding comment kept
   verbatim (it already described this wiring).
3. **`plan.html:100`** — `<script defer src="planner.js">` → `planner.min.js`. (`plan.html` already
   loaded `translations.min.js`; only its planner reference was raw.)

   In all three: `defer`, attribute order, and script **order** are byte-identical to before. Order is
   load-bearing — React → translations → Mixpanel stub → `analytics.js` → planner — and CLAUDE.md
   requires `analytics.js` to stay statically deferred ahead of the planner's first tracking call.

4. **`test_min_asset_boot.js`** (new, 287 lines, port 8862) — rendered Playwright acceptance in the
   house pattern (local static server, vendored React, fixture-routed external hosts, `IGNORABLE`
   error filter). 18 assertions across five scenarios, each checking **both** layers:

   | Scenario | Request-level | Behavior-level (proves the bundle *executes*) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `plan.html` | `planner.min.js` requested, `planner.js` never | `.gp-chip` present; click → `.gp-thread-row` appears |
   | `home.html?fresh=1` | `planner.min.js` + `translations.min.js`, raw never | same chip-click → thread-row proof |
   | `home.html?pool=<id>` | both min, raw never | both north-star CTAs render ("Garden this pool", "Start Earning on …") |
   | `home.html?token=USDC` | both min, raw never | `.pool-card` count > 0 (sacred SEO path) |
   | `plan.html?lang=ko` | `translations.min.js`, raw never | KO copy renders in `.gp-question` |

   The raw-vs-min check is exact-pathname (`urls.includes('/planner.js')`), not substring — so
   `/planner.min.js` can never vacuously satisfy the "raw was never requested" assertion. The verifier
   checked this specifically, including evaluating the predicate by hand.

5. **`package.json`** — `node test_min_asset_boot.js` inserted immediately after
   `node test_minified_assets.js`. Only line touched; dependency blocks untouched.

## Why this is safe (and how that was proven, not assumed)

`minify-assets.js:30` calls terser with `{ compress: true, mangle: true }` and never sets `toplevel`,
so top-level/global names are not mangled — the cross-file globals (`window.TRANSLATIONS`/`t()`,
`Analytics`, the planner mount) survive minification. That is the reason to *expect* the swap to be
behavior-neutral. The rendered test is what *proves* it: real chromium, real DOM, an interactive step
completed on each page.

Staleness is now guarded from both sides: CI regenerates + commits the `.min.` outputs daily
(`sitemap-update.yml:66,149`), and `test_minified_assets.js`'s first 7 assertions fail if any committed
`.min.` file drifts from its source. That gate matters again now — while nothing loaded the bundles,
forgetting `npm run minify` was harmless in prod; after this item it is not.

## Deviations from the spec

**One, documented and defended.** The spec's AC4 said "bare `/` (planner mode)". Reading `home.html`'s
router (`home.html:72-82`), a paramless `/` sets `__APP_MODE = 'landing'` — the search-first landing
shipped 2026-07-15 (LOG item #237/114) — not `'planner'`. CLAUDE.md's "bare `/` = planner" line is
stale (flagged, human-owned, not edited here). The builder used `/?fresh=1`, the minimal
`PLANNER_PARAMS` key that reaches the router's planner branch on `home.html`, which exercises exactly
what AC4 cares about (the swapped tags + the planner mounting from the minified bundle) without
asserting something false about today's bare `/`. The verifier re-read the router source and
independently confirmed the claim.

## What this item did NOT fix (deliberately)

`npm test` now clears files 1–8 and stops at file 9, `test_smoke.js`, on three "bare `/` renders planner
UI" timeouts — the same stale-IA assertions as above, proven identical on a stashed baseline by both
the builder and the verifier. Out of scope here (one item, one red class). It is the obvious next
promotion: `test_landing.js` already asserts the *correct* current behavior for bare `/`, so
`test_smoke.js`'s planner assertions should be retired or repointed. Also untouched:
`test_waitlist_funnel.js`'s 3 known-red cases, and CLAUDE.md's stale IA line.

## Compound step

New playbook `playbooks/pre-existing-red-triage.md` — because the expensive part of this item was not
the three-line fix, it was that eleven loops proved the red *pre-existing* and none *classified* it.
The playbook turns that into a checklist: prove-not-mine → find the `&&`-chain position (that number is
the item's real score) → classify as **A** product regression / **B** stale test / **C** sandbox
environment → and always record how far the chain gets afterward.

## Quiz (answers base64 at the bottom)

1. The three-line swap saves ~159 KB on `home.html`. Why was payload **not** the biggest cost of the bug?
   (A) It was — payload was the whole point · (B) Because Vercel gzips anyway · (C) Because the failing
   freshness test sat at position 6 of a ~90-file `&&` chain and hid every test after it · (D) Because
   the raw files are cached by the service worker

2. What makes it reasonable to expect terser's `mangle: true` not to break `window.TRANSLATIONS`,
   `Analytics`, or the planner mount — and what actually proved it?
   (A) Terser never mangles anything without an explicit list · (B) `toplevel` is unset, so top-level
   names are not mangled — and a real-chromium rendered test proved execution · (C) The bundles are
   only loaded after `DOMContentLoaded` · (D) `compress: true` disables mangling

3. Why does `test_min_asset_boot.js` use `/?fresh=1` instead of a bare `/` for planner mode on
   `home.html`?
   (A) A bare `/` is slower to load · (B) `fresh=1` bypasses the snapshot cache · (C) Playwright cannot
   request a paramless URL · (D) `home.html`'s router resolves a paramless `/` to `__APP_MODE='landing'`
   since the 2026-07-15 search-first-landing pivot; `fresh` is the minimal `PLANNER_PARAMS` key

4. Now that the pages actually load the `.min.` bundles, what stops a source edit from silently shipping
   a stale bundle?
   (A) CI regenerates and commits the `.min.` outputs daily · (B) Vercel minifies at the edge ·
   (C) `test_minified_assets.js` fails if a committed `.min.` file is not byte-identical to a fresh
   minify of its source · (D) Nothing — it is a known risk

5. `npm test` still exits non-zero after this item. Where does it stop, and does that make the item a
   failure?
   (A) At `test_minified_assets.js` — yes, the fix did not work · (B) At `test_smoke.js` (file 9, up

   stashed baseline — not caused here, filed as the follow-up · (C) At `test_waitlist_funnel.js`, which
   this item broke · (D) It stops randomly depending on sandbox network
